memory_candidates.content: When a task description ships a pre-computed classification of a failing gate's items, treat it as a hypothesis with a timestamp, not as input data. Re-measure the live failure set before editing: commits landing between task creation and dispatch routinely add members (here a fourth anchor, app:ObjectiveModality, arrived with a later paper-name correspondence table, so fixing only the three named anchors would have left the gate red) and resolve members the description called blocked (here the cross-repo paper coordination it demanded had already landed, and the 'LIVE BUT UNLABELLED' and 'missing appendix section' claims were both false against the live source). The plan-side carrier is a Scope Hypothesis line on the measuring phase, which makes the measured set authoritative over the report.

An anchor is not pinnable in specs/paper-definitions-of-record.md just because it has a live \label{}. resolve_env (scripts/check-paper-definitions.sh) reads the environment name off the SAME LINE as the \label{}, so a sectioning label on its own line (\subsection{...}% then \label{...}) can never resolve — record it LIVE-UNPINNED, following the app:TaskSemantics precedent. Separately, a theorem-environment anchor whose \begin{proof} block is what the Lean tree actually discusses is pinnable but pointless: resolve_env captures only \begin{Tthm}..\end{Tthm}, so the pin would hash text the tree never quotes. Check which text the citing docstring engages with, not just whether a label exists.
